hypotheses.statement: Customers wait because there is no fast channel to get refund status answers; a chatbot answering routine questions would reduce the wait.

checks.detail: The stated root_problem text accurately reflects E-01 (5/5 IBAN failures) and E-02 (2.0h median vs 24h SLA) without overstating certainty beyond what the sample and aggregate show.

output.summary: The stakeholder SH-SUP requested a chatbot to stop customers 'waiting forever' for refund answers (CL-01, CL-02, E-03), but the investigation (PD-1) found the real driver is a payment-data defect, not slow support: all 5 sampled refund_failures were FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01, F-01) while support's median response time is 2.0h against a 24h SLA across 900 tickets (E-02, F-02). What was actually released is the two datasets (ticket-db response_times and payment-db refund_failures, work items W-WI-TICKET-DATASET and W-WI-REFUND-FAILURE-DATASET) produced for the labeled deliverable 'quantify_iban_failure_ticket_correlation', not a chatbot and not any IBAN data correction. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS and verification found the two source datasets share no common key, so the labeled 'correlation' cannot actually be computed as described, among other open items.
key_points: The chatbot premise (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-INFO-GAP, supported only by stakeholder claim E-03) was rejected because it is contradicted by E-01 and E-02; the supported hypothesis is H-REFUND-IBAN-FAILURE, that refund-wait tickets stem from IBAN-format payment failures, not slow answering.

Released scope matches solution_design.release_scope and minimum_useful_scope: the DA-TCK and DA-PAY datasets for quantify_iban_failure_ticket_correlation; the intended_scope action correct_invalid_iban_records:DA-PAY was not released.

A verification check (seq 97, semantic:correlation_label_vs_feasibility, work item W-WI-CORRELATION-FEASIBILITY-C) found ticket-db response_times and payment-db refund_failures share no common key, so a true per-ticket correlation cannot be computed even though the deliverable is still labeled a correlation.
The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS (seq 58), deferring the critical unknown U-FAILURE-TICKET-OVERLAP to VOB-U-FAILURE-TICKET-OVERLAP rather than resolving it before release.

Two solution remedies that would address the root cause (SR-CORRECT-IBAN-DATA: fix invalid IBANs; SR-ADD-IBAN-VALIDATION-CONTROL: add validation at refund submission, process P-REF) were marked not feasible in contest time and remain unfinished.
Success criteria SC-NO-CHATBOT-WITHOUT-CAUSE-FIX and SC-NO-SPEED-CREDIT explicitly bar crediting the problem's resolution to chatbot speed, consistent with the data-driven root-cause finding.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, with the critical unknown of ticket-failure overlap deferred as a verification obligation (VOB-U-FAILURE-TICKET-OVERLAP) rather than answered before release.

The deliverable is labeled a ticket-failure correlation, but ticket-db response_times and payment-db refund_failures have no shared key field, so a true per-ticket correlation cannot actually be computed from this data (W-WI-CORRELATION-FEASIBILITY-C).
VOB-U-FAILURE-TICKET-OVERLAP is still open and blocks the IBAN-correction scope (correct_invalid_iban_records:DA-PAY), which falls outside what was released.
VOB-R-2 is open: it is unverified whether the 5-record refund_failures sample is representative of the full population, since DA-PAY completeness is marked UNKNOWN (U-SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS).

No FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds were actually corrected, and no validation control was added at refund submission (process P-REF); both remedies (SR-CORRECT-IBAN-DATA, SR-ADD-IBAN-VALIDATION-CONTROL) were assessed as infeasible in contest time.

Even if the IBAN defect is confirmed material, any future correction would only cover the 5 sampled records (R-0..R-4), not unsampled or future failures, and no population-level failure rate has been established.
